title: Constipation and Malaise - Internal Medicine Case
hpi_narrative: A 65-year-old male with no significant past medical history presents with constipation and malaise. The onset of symptoms is unknown, the character and severity are moderate, associated symptoms include nausea and vomiting, pertinent negatives include no reported fever or weight loss. The single clinical question this case forces you to answer is whether the patient has colon cancer and if so, to what extent it has spread.

stacks.finding: A colonoscopy would be warranted so that a biopsy may be taken from the mass that was found on imaging for diagnostic confirmation. A sigmoidoscopy or a flexible sigmoidoscopy does not cover enough of the colon to verify if a patient does or does not have polyps/cancer. Patients should undergo a full colonoscopy before surgery for colon cancer.
